access_timestamp_note: Observed UTC clock immediately after retrieval batch; web retrieval tool exposes no per-page fetch timestamp.
source_id_policy: IDs are stable within this stage. Never silently rebind an ID; append a new ID if a different source is used.
discovery_basis: Independent public-source research from brief.md only; exact plan not read before the assigned reveal step.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Process receipts and deliveries with barcodes
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified on page.
sources.locator: Barcode app; Scan barcodes for receipts; Validating the delivery; full page.
sources.observed_operation: The documented flow opens Operations, selects an outstanding receipt, scans the transfer/products, and uses Validate to proceed with stock moves.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Barcode feature must be enabled. The described operation is real-time; page does not document offline queueing.
sources.applicability: Reference for shipment/receipt-first operations. It does not establish a reusable-crate identity model or offline support.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Operation types and commands
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified.
sources.locator: Use barcodes for inventory operations and commands; Receipts WHIN warning.
sources.observed_operation: A receipt operation barcode WHIN always creates a new operation instance; a scheduled receipt must be opened from its individual picking barcode.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default printed operation types include Receipts WHIN where Barcode is enabled. Exception: scan the specific picking to reach an existing scheduled receipt.
sources.applicability: Consequential guard for staff so a generic command is not mistaken for a shipment-specific receipt.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Product and location barcodes
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified.
sources.locator: Barcode nomenclature; Barcode lookup; Configure product barcode.
sources.observed_operation: Odoo supports arbitrary strings as internal references. Creating a new GS1 GTIN requires a GS1 Company Prefix; Stock Barcode Database lookup is a separately enabled option for UPC/EAN/ISBN.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Custom strings are internal-use references. External GTIN allocation is distinct; database lookup is opt-in.
sources.applicability: Supports considering a local coop namespace without buying allocations, while warning against treating SKU/GTIN lookup as crate identity.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Barcodes for lot and serial numbers
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified.
sources.locator: Mandatory and optional scanning; damaged vendor lot/serial label tip.
sources.observed_operation: Each operation type can set lot/serial scan to mandatory or optional; optional scan allows manual typing and the docs recommend optional scan where received labels may be damaged.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Setting is configurable per operation type; mandatory scan blocks manual entry for required serial/lot.
sources.applicability: A relevant fallback precedent for damaged labels, though it addresses serial/lot tracking, not this coop's crate identifier.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Default barcode nomenclature
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified.
sources.locator: Default barcode nomenclature; rule matching and custom rules.
sources.observed_operation: Barcode nomenclature checks rules in order; prefix and/or length patterns determine a matching rule, and custom patterns are supported.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: First matching rule wins; custom rules may classify strings, but fields do not automatically populate merely because a rule exists.
sources.applicability: Shows parser precedence can change interpretation; reserve a non-overlapping internal namespace and test the deployed rules.

sources.title: Odoo 18.0 — Connect a printer / barcode scanner
sources.version_or_commit: Versioned Odoo documentation: 18.0; product patch/build is not specified.
sources.locator: Barcode scanner issues: scanner detected as keyboard; characters individually; incorrect keyboard layout.
sources.observed_operation: Docs say some scanners are seen as USB keyboards, keyboard layout affects input, and some mobile/IoT setups may treat each character as a separate scan.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Behavior depends on scanner, keyboard layout, mobile version, and IoT pairing; a separate Is scanner setting is needed for certain IoT cases.
sources.applicability: Supports an inexpensive keyboard-emulating reader as a possibility, not a compatibility guarantee. Test actual model/host/language/terminator.

sources.title: Snipe-IT — Asset Tags
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; page has no release binding. Current repository release context is v8.8.0 (commit 2c466fa), separately recorded as S04.
sources.locator: Unique asset tag; auto-incrementing IDs; prefix; Length of Asset Tags.
sources.observed_operation: An asset tag must be unique within Snipe-IT; optional prefix and zero-fill are available; changing length does not update existing tags.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Zero-fill standardizes new length but is not a migration of already stored tags; mixed alphanumeric tags can confuse numeric auto-increment.
sources.applicability: Useful asset-ID analogue and direct warning to freeze the pilot namespace or plan explicit migration/alias handling.

sources.title: Snipe-IT — Asset Labels
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version shown. Page indicates an update six months before access; current release context Snipe-IT v8.8.0 is separately S04.
sources.locator: 1D and 2D labels; QR; USB/Bluetooth scanner; barcode setting.
sources.observed_operation: Labels can carry 1D and 2D codes; QR opens an in-system asset link on a mobile reader; bottom 1D barcode searches by asset tag; standard USB/Bluetooth scanner described.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Barcode feature must be enabled. QR target is the Snipe-IT asset page, not an authorized public care page.
sources.applicability: Supports dual-code label design as an analogue, but do not expose private asset URL or movement history through the coop's public QR.

sources.title: Snipe-IT — Importing Assets
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version shown.
sources.locator: Mapping Asset Fields; ID; Asset Tag; Serial.
sources.observed_operation: For asset-tag change on import, internal ID is required; otherwise asset tag is used to look up the record. Serial is a separate field.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: When an internal ID is provided it supersedes tag lookup; asset tag may be auto-generated if configured.
sources.applicability: Illustrates why database-row ID, physical asset tag, and manufacturer serial should not be conflated.

sources.title: Snipe-IT release v8.8.0
sources.version_or_commit: Snipe-IT v8.8.0, tag commit 2c466fa; released 2026-09-30.
sources.locator: Release overview lines 153-170; What's Changed lines 311 and 326; docs-updating note line 270.
sources.observed_operation: Release lists the QR text transfer fix for the New Label Engine and 1D barcode support for a Zebra label template; official mobile app and sync adapters are described as beta; release says docs are being updated.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These are features/fixes in this release; beta status does not establish stable offline event queueing.
sources.applicability: Provides current release context for rolling docs and confirms label output changed recently; verify exact release behavior rather than generalizing.

sources.title: Snipe-IT issue #19515 — QR Code Text missing in New Label Engine
sources.version_or_commit: Issue reports Snipe-IT v8.7.1; opened 2026-08-18; closed 2026-09-23 after fix commit c1d1cd1.
sources.locator: Description; Snipe-IT Version; linked PR and close activity.
sources.observed_operation: Reporter says old QR Code Text setting was not carried into the New Label Engine; field was not visible and blank text could result in no QR output.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported during legacy-to-new label-engine transition; this is a specific product migration issue.
sources.applicability: Direct caution for QR label configuration migrations. Not a general QR or scanner defect.

sources.title: Snipe-IT PR #19633 — code diff for QR text transfer
sources.version_or_commit: Commit 1e0fc8c (change), merged commit c1d1cd1 on 2026-09-17 into develop; fix appears in v8.8.0.
sources.locator: SettingsController.php transition logic and labels-new-engine view diff.
sources.observed_operation: When the new label engine becomes enabled from disabled, code copies stored qr_text to label2_title; explanatory UI help is removed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Copy is performed once on the transition, not a general migration of every label field.
sources.applicability: Primary code-level evidence for migration behavior; test persisted config plus decoded generated samples after an engine switch.

sources.title: Snipe-IT PR #19679 — 1D barcode support for Zebra template
sources.version_or_commit: Commit df2c3d8, merged 2026-09-23 into develop; included in v8.8.0 release notes.
sources.locator: PR description and merge metadata.
sources.observed_operation: Adds a 1D barcode to one Zebra label template (template 18939).
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to the named label template, not all printers/templates.
sources.applicability: Evidence that specific template output can differ; print-sample checks need the actual printer/template combination.

sources.title: GS1 Digital Link Quick Start Guide
sources.version_or_commit: Official GS1 guide dated by URL/publication as 2024; no point version shown.
sources.locator: Sections 2-5: offline identifier vs web access, application identifiers, identifier vs page URL, redirects.
sources.observed_operation: Guide describes a QR with GS1 Digital Link URI as parseable with GS1 identifiers offline and also followable by a generic camera as a web link; GTIN, lot/serial qualifier examples use a defined hierarchy.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: GS1 application identifiers have defined rules; serial/lot qualifiers are combined with an appropriate primary key. Web target retrieval is separate from local decode.
sources.applicability: Analogous identifier/resolver architecture only; does not grant or establish a cooperative crate ID or justify buying an allocation.

sources.title: GS1 — Redirection: from scan to content
sources.version_or_commit: Official GS1 guidance, copyright 2024; no point version shown.
sources.locator: Pages 1-3: organizational split, redirects, domain ownership, analytics, 303 recommendation.
sources.observed_operation: GS1 says identifier and information location are distinct; redirect target can move; it recommends temporary 303 redirects and describes scan services that may collect time, place, and device analytics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance assumes GS1 Digital Link URI for formal sections; outside GS1, QR shorteners/analytics are separate service choices.
sources.applicability: Supports web-owner governance and warns against accidental location/device analytics in the public care flow.

sources.title: GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard 1.2.0
sources.version_or_commit: Release 1.2.0, ratified January 2026.
sources.locator: Sections 4 and 5; resolver independence, redirect behavior, 404 and HTTPS/CORS requirements.
sources.observed_operation: Different conformant resolvers are not required to yield identical targets/linksets; standard defines redirect/linkset behavior and resolver description metadata.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Requirements apply to a GS1-conformant resolver and supported GS1 keys; syntactically valid identifier with no entity info returns 404.
sources.applicability: If a GS1 resolver is ever selected, owner must govern the resolver/domain and target. For this pilot, a simpler coop-owned HTTPS page/link is enough.

sources.title: GS1 General Specifications 23.0.0
sources.version_or_commit: GS1 General Specifications release 23.0.0.
sources.locator: QR Code symbology identifier and FNC1 / GS1 QR notes.
sources.observed_operation: Standard identifies ]Q3 as symbology identifier for GS1 QR codes with leading FNC1.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This marker distinguishes a GS1-system QR path; it is metadata/format information, not a receipt event or offline queue.
sources.applicability: Use only if the selected decoder/parser requires GS1 symbology identification; test exact reader output.

sources.title: ZXing PR #1681 — update GS1 AIs to 2023 spec
sources.version_or_commit: Commit 557b5fc; merged 2023-09-04; milestone 3.5.3.
sources.locator: Conversation description, compatibility note, milestone.
sources.observed_operation: Parser updates length limits where GS1 spec increased lengths; where lengths decreased or identifiers were removed, code remains permissive for backward compatibility.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies to ZXing's GS1 AI parsing and its 2023 spec update; not all barcode libraries.
sources.applicability: Format-migration example; pin parser version and test supported current plus legacy payloads only if adopting GS1 parsing.

sources.title: ZXing PR #1839 — preserve QRCodeMultiReader symbology identifier
sources.version_or_commit: Commit 34588d8; merged 2024-08-02.
sources.locator: Background/change/technical details.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Relevant when using ZXing QRCodeMultiReader and downstream processing depends on the symbology marker; single-reader and other scanner stacks differ.
sources.applicability: Narrow decoder behavior change; propose exact metadata regression test only if this code path is selected.

sources.title: Snipe-IT — Managing Assets
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version shown; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Best Practices — Checking out assets to non-people.
sources.observed_operation: Snipe-IT says asset checkouts can target a location or another asset but discourages non-person targets because they cannot be accountable for damage/loss.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is stated best-practice guidance, not a technical prohibition; location checkout remains possible.
sources.applicability: A depot-as-location checkout is supported but may not fit custody accountability. Keep movement/receipt event modeling explicit rather than mapping every depot move to a checkout.

sources.title: Snipe-IT — Overview
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling official documentation; no release version shown; accessed 2026-10-10.
sources.locator: Assets; Asset Tags; Checkin/Checkout.
sources.observed_operation: Snipe-IT describes unique asset tags and check-in/check-out as its asset custody process; location checkout is possible but not recommended for accountability.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Docs discuss ordinary asset checkout lifecycle; no coop-specific shipment receipt behavior or offline queue is specified.
sources.applicability: Supports Snipe-IT as an asset workflow analogue while bounding its fit for crate movements.
